```
G1: reads c.data[key] (line 44, no lock)
G2: writes c.data[key] = ... (line 95, Set method, no lock)
```

## Corrective Precedents

```go
// Use sync.RWMutex for read-heavy workloads
mu sync.RWMutex

// Use atomic counters
stats struct {
    Hits, Misses, LoadErrors atomic.Int64
}

// Set must acquire lock
func (c *Cache) Set(key string, value interface{}) {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    c.data[key] = &CacheEntry{...}
}

// GetMulti must use WaitGroup and mutex for results
func (c *Cache) GetMulti(ctx context.Context, keys []string) map[string]interface{} {
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    var mu sync.Mutex
    results := make(map[string]interface{})
    for _, key := range keys {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func(k string) {
            defer wg.Done()
            if v, err := c.Get(ctx, k); err == nil {
                mu.Lock()
                results[k] = v
                mu.Unlock()
            }
        }(key)
    }
    wg.Wait()
    return results
}

// cleanup must hold lock during iteration
func (c *Cache) cleanup() {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    // iterate and delete
}

// waitForLoad needs condition variable, not busy-wait
```

We coordinate according to precedent: `sync.RWMutex` for the map, `atomic` for counters, `sync.Cond` for waiters, and **never** access shared state without synchronization.

This is how it has been done. This is how it will be done.
